samples.question: The picture shows eight combs on a plain background. A comb is a group of three solid vertical teeth of equal width standing side by side on one common baseline, so within a comb only the heights of the teeth differ. Four combs are pressed against the left edge of the page in one column and form the left ledger; the other four are pressed against the right edge in one column and form the right ledger. The wide middle of the page is empty, and nothing joins the two ledgers. Counting downwards from the top of the left ledger its combs are the first, second, third and fourth. The signature of a comb is its three tooth heights read from left to right, where the height of a tooth is how far it rises above its comb's baseline. Exactly one comb in the left ledger has the same signature as one comb in the right ledger: all three of its teeth match that far comb's three teeth in the same left-to-right order. Every other pairing of a left comb with a right comb differs by a clearly visible amount in at least one of the three teeth, and the picture always contains decoy pairs that agree on two of their three teeth and disagree on the third, so a comb that only half matches is not the answer. Both ledgers must be read: the left ledger alone never reveals which of its combs is repeated, and the right ledger alone never names a row. Which row of the right ledger holds the repeat, the ink colour, how far each ledger sits from its edge, the small up and down shifts of the baselines, and the isolated specks scattered in the background all carry no information. Which comb of the left ledger has its signature repeated by a comb of the right ledger? Answer with one of: first, second, third, fourth.
